propositions: The bugfix-size gate blocks large bug fixes (>150 non-test lines) that carry a passed plan-review attestation signed by unpinned developer environments because the not-pinned arm of classify_plan_review_attestation returns a mismatch verdict, which is a FLAG verdict that blocks.

The gate's cross-host verification design requires the DSSE principal to be pinned in .rebar/trusted_environments.yaml, but developer plan reviews are signed with unpinned developer environment IDs, making the criterion unsatisfiable for any locally-reviewed bug.

The op-cert service exists but there is no client in the repo to call it, no mechanism to persist its returned envelope as a ticket attestation, and the service guard is a production secret in SSM, so obtaining a prod-attested plan review is not an executable path for contributors.

The fix removes the cross-host provenance check (trusted_env_keyring lookup and verify_opcert call) and gates only on the fact of a completed, subject-bound, lifecycle-valid plan-review attestation, re-asserting subject binding explicitly in classify_plan_review_attestation.

The attestation record lives on the attacker-writable tickets branch with no cryptographic trust root for unpinned signers, so this criterion becomes an anti-sloppiness gate rather than an anti-adversary one, with the adversarial boundary remaining at LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 votes on the Gerrit-gated code branch.

The fix is demonstrated end-to-end on real Gerrit changes (1344/129e blocked, 1404 merged) with documented executable path: rebar review-plan run locally in developer environment, signature read from signed payload, no op-cert service or admin round-trip required.
